title: Falling Cape Freight Rates: Guinea's Bauxite Shipments Move from a Test of Resilience to a Test of Elasticity
section_path: Falling Cape Freight Rates: Guinea's Bauxite Shipments Move from a Test of Resilience to a Test of Elasticity
section_path_text: Falling Cape Freight Rates: Guinea's Bauxite Shipments Move from a Test of Resilience to a Test of Elasticity
summary:
Main
Image reference: assets/2026-10-16_falling-cape-freight-rates-guineas-bauxite-shipments-move-from-a-test-of-resilie_img_rgb-color-brs-shipbrokers-monogram-l_c365f35f1de5.png
One notable development in the recent dry bulk market has been the sharp retreat in Capesize freight rates from elevated levels, contrasting with the relatively steady to firmer performance of Panamaxes and Supramaxes. According to Baltic Exchange indices, Cape 5TC (182k) fell from a high of $58,294/day on 4 Sep to $37,618/day across one month, a decline of 35%. By comparison, the Panamax and Supramax indices fell 1% and rose 15%, respectively, thus significantly outperforming Capesize in the same time period (4 Sep - 12 Oct).
